- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent periods.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) or shows strong reversal, model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply mean reversion bias: forecast = prior + 0.7×(true - prior) for next period.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; use 10-day moving average of true values as baseline for correction.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7), model tends to err on the high side; apply 1–2% downward adjustment to forecast.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- For low sentiment (≤0.2), model often ignores downward pressure; apply 2–5% downward bias if true outcome is below 10% of 30-day average.
